clue.text: Sign of some production

parts.note: surface reading: an indication that something is being made or staged
setter's reading: the registered symbol a manufacturer puts on its goods

explanation.walkthrough: 'Production' suggests a show or a process; read it as a producer's goods, and the sign is the badge identifying whose they are.
explanation.definitionFit: A trademark is a registered symbol or name that identifies goods as coming from one particular maker.

clue.text: Academic library user?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a senior university lecturer ranked just below professor in Britain
second meaning: someone who reads books

explanation.walkthrough: In British universities a Reader is an academic rank between senior lecturer and professor; the question mark flags that the library user is just one example of a person who reads.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a university job title and the general term for a person who reads, such as a library borrower.

clue.text: Scribble old ode badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters before it are put together in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on someone's old poem: it is a badly written scrawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To doodle is to scribble idly, drawing aimless marks on paper.

clue.text: Painter, philosopher and economist — and French, too!

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was both a philosopher and an economist
et is French for 'and', which the clue renders as 'too'

explanation.surface: A list of a polymath's talents, ending with the surprise that he was French as well.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter is Jean-François Millet, who was indeed French; 'and French, too' means the French word for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-François Millet was a nineteenth-century French artist famous for paintings of peasant life such as The Gleaners.

clue.text: Circulate and tour here

indicators.note: to circulate is to go round, so the following letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to stroll round a building and take a look.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a rotunda is a round building, just the place to walk in a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a circular building or hall, usually domed, so going round it is exactly what visitors do.

clue.text: Listens again to a line for practice

parts.note: re-hears: hears a second time
taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An actor going over a line again and again to get it right.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice session held before a performance.

clue.text: Use me as an alternative to the cane!

definitions.text: Use me as an alternative to the cane!

parts.words: Use me as an alternative to the cane!
parts.note: surface reading: a punishment offered instead of a caning

parts.words: Use me as an alternative to the cane!
parts.note: setter's reading: a crop grown for sweetening as well as sugar cane

explanation.walkthrough: The cane looks like a schoolmaster's rod, and the answer's second word seems to fit that picture of a thrashing; really it is sugar cane, and the alternative crop is a root vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar beet is the root crop that supplies much of the world's sugar besides sugar cane.

clue.text: Backs order to send brief

indicators.note: an order to arrange things means the letters that follow are put into a fresh sequence

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sponsor instructs that the paperwork be sent to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' reads as a noun at first, but it is the verb: supports.
explanation.definitionFit: To befriend someone is to act as a friend to them, supporting or standing behind them.

clue.text: Read for each application

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per person'
an application of something is a use of it

explanation.surface: Instructions to read every application form that comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read something through carefully.

clue.text: You'll find French sleepers in and under these

definitions.text: You'll find French sleepers in and under these

parts.words: You'll find French sleepers in and under these
parts.note: surface reading: beds where people from France sleep

parts.words: You'll find French sleepers in and under these
parts.note: setter's reading: railway sleeping cars, with passengers asleep inside and wooden track sleepers beneath

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleepers' works twice: passengers dozing in the carriages, and the wooden beams under the rails on which the carriages run.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagons-lits are sleeping cars on continental European trains, the French term for railway carriages fitted with beds.

clue.text: Go to a place to make good

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to betake oneself somewhere
second meaning: to fix or mend

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a formal, old-fashioned verb: to repair to a place is simply to go there.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two unrelated senses: formally, to go somewhere, and commonly, to mend what is damaged.

clue.text: Fit? Begin training to reach a healthy state

parts.note: fit and well both mean in good health

indicators.note: training shapes something into a new form, so the word before it is reshaped

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fitness coach urges a client to start exercising to become healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-being is the condition of being comfortable, healthy and content.

clue.text: A baler required for this kind of field

definitions.text: A baler required for this kind of field

indicators.note: read loosely as re-quired, needed afresh, it hints that the preceding letters must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer notes that a field of this type needs a baling machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a baler, which packs hay or straw into bales, is needed on cropland; the anagram signal is a weak one.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is ploughed and used for growing crops, which is where balers are put to work at harvest.

clue.text: Performed for one day, possibly showing composure

parts.note: a singer performed, that is sang

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the word it follows is rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A singer who performed for a day kept calm throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Sang-froid, French for 'cold blood', is coolness and self-possession under pressure.

clue.text: Religious book (English) has spine repaired

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An English Bible is sent to the bookbinder to have its spine mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesians is a book of the New Testament, Paul's epistle to the church at Ephesus.

clue.text: Test rig to get repaired, being in the worst condition

indicators.note: a repaired machine has been taken apart and put together again, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
also part of the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of testing equipment is sent for repair because it is in such poor shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' does double work here: it is part of the letters rearranged, so only 'get' and 'being' join the parts. Grotty is British slang for shabby or nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotty is British slang for unpleasant or shabby, so the grottiest thing is the one in the worst state.

clue.text: "Attention" in the army

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A sergeant-major's bark of 'Attention!' on the parade ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attention' looks like a drill command, but it means the act of listening.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone your ear is to give them your attention.

clue.text: A river of one's knowledge

indicators.note: of here means made of, taking letters out from the words that follow

parts.note: the tail of the first word joins the head of the second

explanation.surface: A geography question: name a river you happen to know.
explanation.walkthrough: The Esk is the name of several rivers in England and Scotland, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: The Esk is a river name found in Yorkshire, Cumbria and Scotland.

clue.text: Criticise a sort of pop music

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a style of rhythmic spoken lyrics over a beat

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single complaint about pop, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To rap someone is to rebuke them sharply, and rap is also a genre of rhythmic spoken music.

clue.text: Church feature in a society with hopes for the future

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the pair of letters that follow it

parts.note: taken as written
a spire is the tapering top of a church tower
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A church spire seen as a symbol of a community's hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to hope or aim for something in the future.

clue.text: Quite exhausted when it's all over

definitions.meaning: first meaning: with nothing left, as in being at the end of one's tether

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tiredness after an event, but the phrase works both as worn out and as finished.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means finished or concluded, and of a person's resources, used up completely.

clue.text: Half the fish go to sleep

indicators.note: half means only the first part of the word is kept and the rest is discarded

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: Someone eats half their fish supper and then nods off.
explanation.walkthrough: Kip is British slang for sleep, used as a verb as well as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Kip is British slang for sleep, so to kip is to go to sleep.

clue.text: Topic (watches, say) — make a list

parts.note: an item on an agenda is a topic

indicators.note: say signals that the word before it is to be heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: eyes are what one watches with, and the word sounds like these letters

explanation.surface: An agenda item about watches, and a request to draw up a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watches' looks like timepieces but stands for eyes, the organs that watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to set things out one by one as a list.

clue.text: Course at Oxford gets on one's nerves, they say

indicators.note: they say points to what is heard spoken, so the word is spelt differently from how it sounds

parts.note: something that grates on you irritates you

explanation.surface: A student grumbling that their Oxford course is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: Greats is the informal name for Literae Humaniores, the classics degree at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Greats is the traditional Oxford name for the degree course in classics, ancient history and philosophy.

clue.text: Totally occupy one parking spur

parts.note: to fill a space is to occupy all of it
I is the Roman numeral for one
P is the road-sign symbol for parking

explanation.surface: A driver takes up an entire parking space on a slip road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spur' suggests a branch road near the parking, but it is a noun meaning a stimulus.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a boost or stimulus, something that spurs a person or activity on.

clue.text: Cable about washer

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the letters of the next word are moved around

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wiring query concerning a small ring used on a cable fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or steel cable used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: It's gained for service on the part of the hospital

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a business letter
a ward is a room or section of a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital worker is honoured for long service in one department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the part' reads as a set phrase, but 'on' is a separate piece meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something given in return for good work or service rendered.

clue.text: Possibly decimated, as people are by taking pills

definitions.text: as people are by taking pills

indicators.note: possibly hints at another way of arranging the word next to it

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dark suggestion that pill-taking might wipe out a population.
explanation.definitionFit: People who take pills are treated with drugs, which is what being medicated means.

clue.text: Mainly cultivating fruit

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: raising crops is cultivating them

explanation.surface: A farmer who mostly grows fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a common dried fruit.

clue.text: One acting as cover?

parts.note: surface reading: a stand-in, an understudy or an undercover agent
setter's reading: a cricketer placed at the fielding position called cover

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, cover is a fielding position on the off side of the pitch, so the player stationed there is literally acting as cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A fieldsman is a cricket player on the fielding side, and cover point is one of the positions such a player takes.

clue.text: Iodine is one mixture able to produce charged particles

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

indicators.note: a mixture is things stirred together, so the words before it are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: an iodine mixture can create charged particles.
explanation.definitionFit: To ionise is to convert atoms into ions, which are electrically charged particles.

clue.text: Dread pose adopted by outlaw

indicators.note: a pose that is adopted is taken on in a new form, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain strikes a frightening stance.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless, violent criminal, the classic Wild West outlaw.
